title: Globular Cluster Omega Centauri
explanation:
# Omega Centauri: A Cosmic Puzzle

Omega Centauri, the largest and brightest star cluster orbiting our Milky Way, is a dense ball of roughly 10 million ancient stars packed into a space 150 light-years across, located 15,000 light-years away. What makes this stellar swarm so strange is that unlike typical star clusters born together in matching families, Omega Centauri contains stars of different ages and chemical compositions—a signature that hints it might be the leftover heart of a small galaxy that collided with our own, now harboring a supermassive black hole at its center.
